7.text: After the five days, the head of the polar bear is cooked in a big

8.text: kettle, and then a feast is arranged, to which all the neighbors are invited.

9.text: The meat of the head must be entirely eaten.

10.text: An analogous custom in regard to the brown bear is found among the Lamut.

11.text: The meat of this likewise must be boiled all at once and eaten by the neigh-

12.text: bors of the hunter gathered for the feast, without reserving any for the future.

13.text: A feast, accompanied with a ceremonial dance and shamanistic perform-

14.text: ances both by day and by night, is also arranged for a whale. After the

15.text: feast, all the crumbs, stray hair, etc., are gathered and thrown into the sea,

16.text: which act restores the killed whale to life and to the sea.

17.text: The eyes of the bear and the whale are pierced; and the viscous fluid

35.text: In some of the villages, the family of the chief hunter, after a successful

36.text: hunt of the whale, arrange for a thanksgiving ceremonial at the time of the

37.text: new moon in every month. This lasts during the whole season, for four or five

38.text: consecutive months. On St. Lawrence Island, the successful hunter of the whale

39.text: offers during the ceremonial a sacrifice of the hair of his head, which is thrown

40.text: into the fire of the hearth, and is said to be directed to the giver of whales.
